comparison: Perfect agreement on behavioral findings (C42-C51, C74, C77). Both evaluations rate these claims as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes statistical rigor (t-tests, permutation tests, Bayes factors) and convergent evidence. Peer reviewers explicitly affirmed the behavioral evidence with quotes praising thoroughness and convincing psychometric curves.

Agreement on baseline effects (C59-C62) but different interpretations. OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN due to inconsistent findings across environments and concerns about the selective effect in alternating environment. Peer reviewers rate as SUPPORTED, interpreting the minimal baseline modulation as evidence that adaptive bias unfolds dynamically rather than at baseline.

Strong agreement on the central finding about slope effects (C63-C72, C75, C78-C79). Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes convergent evidence from complementary analyses but flags marginal p-value (p=0.048). Peer reviewers explicitly endorsed this as the key contribution, with all three reviewers affirming the slope-based mechanism.

Perfect agreement on methodological details (C100-C137). Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval acknowledges appropriate use of established software and standard procedures but notes some preprocessing decisions lack justification. Peer reviewers praised the methodological rigor as 'state-of-the-art' and 'elegantly designed' without raising concerns.

Agreement on experimental design quality (C9-C41). Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval provides detailed assessment of quantitative parameters, controls, and balanced design. Peer reviewers affirmed the design as 'well-designed' and 'elegantly designed' with clear methods. High overlap (33 shared claims) with strong concordance.

Agreement on neural characterizations (C52-C58). Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes replication of established signatures and functional validation. Peer reviewers accepted findings as consistent with prior work on decision-making and action planning. OpenEval also addresses spatial leakage concerns (C122-C123) not mentioned in this peer result.

Both address source leakage concerns (C122-C123). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, noting control analyses address spatial leakage. Peer reviewer initially raised concerns but accepted the revised manuscript's explanation that leakage doesn't affect conclusions focused on differences between patches.

Agreement on participant recruitment and sample details (C1-C8). Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval provides detailed assessment of documentation and exclusion criteria, noting lack of quantification for one threshold. Peer reviewers affirmed overall design quality without specific concerns about participant selection.

Agreement on contextualization and novelty (C138-C141). Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes appropriate comparison to prior work and reasonable but speculative inference about flexible signal use. Peer reviewers affirmed novelty and significance, characterizing the work as valuable and impactful.

Partial overlap on contextualization claims (C80, C151). Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval addresses extensive literature citations (C73-C157) for context and mechanistic speculation. Peer reviewers focus on novelty and impact statements, affirming the contribution to the field.

OpenEval evaluated limitation acknowledgment (C142) as SUPPORTED, noting honest assessment of methodological constraints. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this specific limitation claim.
